chapter: Los Angeles, Chet Baker and film beginnings
title: Tiny Kahn, Mel Lewis and the role of taste
summary: Mandel says Mel Lewis modeled himself on Tiny Kahn, and that taste, as with Basie and Sweets, is the arbiter of greatness; Manne's dynamics are admired.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Yeah.

And his sense of sound I don’t think made it for a big-band as well as it did for a small band. Whereas Tiny Kahn was never as great a small band drummer even though he did a lot of small band work as he was a big band drummer.
Well he and Mel Lewis were very close.
Well that was Mel's original inspiration, Tiny, that's who Mel wanted to be like and he was right.
Yeah, they’re not interchangeable, I mean…
No.
You can tell one from the other…
Oh sure, they’re not alike at all.
I don’t know, I hear a certain – there’s an affinity of approach there between…
It was the time sense that Mel had.
Yeah.
That he loved about Tiny. Tiny was a musician with not much technique, just all feel…
The same with Mel…
He wasn’t a great technical drummer, he wasn't a great technical arranger but everything he did was perfect.
Yeah, it’s like…

You know, ‘cause taste is above all the arbiter of greatness I think. Count Basie was – nobody really realized how good a piano player Count Basie was in his early days, he was a terror if you listen to the Bennie Moten things from 1932 on. He played more damn piano than Fats on those records, which is really saying something and never did with his own band that much piano. But the man had such great taste that those few ideas he used to throw around, that if anybody else did you’d be sick of him within a few days, lasted all his life because he had taste like no one did and he had the best time. And Tiny was like that, Sweets is like that.
Yeah, Mel was like that too.
Yeah, Mel had a lot more variety though in his playing.
Yeah.
He could do a lot of things, especially when he got with his own band.
Yeah, the best drum solos I ever heard Mel play were in small groups where – I heard him one night play a brush solo on, “Body and Soul,” done at ballad tempo that was just superb.
Oh, that's the kind of thing Shelly did so well, that kind of thing, shading, and subtleties of playing. He might've been the best drummer when it came to dynamics.
And had wonderful time.
Yeah.
